text: Our scouts glimpsed something of interest nearby, but the army was marching too fast to stop and look. Switch to default stance before returning to the location to take a closer look.
We passed a smithy without stopping. Perhaps a lord should come back to see what it holds.
The Master Blacksmith Is Ready To Receive You
The master blacksmith sends word that the forge is ready again. Send a lord to the smithy to choose from his new work.

We sent the master blacksmith and the garrison an urgent order to retreat, and they obeyed. The enemy has taken the smithy and its forge has lost a level, but our people live to fight another day. We will get the smithy back in time.
Our army has been driven back from the smithy. Its defenders held the forge this time, but a smithy guarded so fiercely is worth taking. We should return with a stronger force.
The enemy broke against the smithy's walls and fled. Our garrison is already dragging the dead from the yard, and by nightfall the forge is burning again.

We lost control of the smithy. We saved the master blacksmith and some of his disciples, but the forge has lost a level, and we lose both its tribute and our visits to it. We should recapture it as soon as we can.
An enemy army has surrounded our smithy. At the start of our turn we must decide whether to defend it or give it up.
We could not raise a garrison in time. The raiders looted the forge before leaving, and it has lost a level of craft.

Our gold has rebuilt the forge and strengthened its garrison. It now stands at [[col:yellow]]level 2 of 3[[/col]]: its free pieces are of [[col:yellow]]uncommon or rare[[/col]] quality, it is ready sooner after each piece, and its tribute arrives more often.

Our gold has rebuilt the forge and strengthened its garrison. It now stands at [[col:yellow]]level 3 of 3[[/col]], the finest it can be: its free pieces are all [[col:yellow]]rare[[/col]], it is ready soonest after each piece, its tribute arrives most often, a commission yields [[col:yellow]]two masterworks[[/col]], and the master blacksmith will now craft a [[col:yellow]]unique piece[[/col]] on commission.

The enemy army has been routed and the smithy is ours. We install our own master blacksmith and a detachment to guard him. The forge stands at [[col:yellow]]level 1 of 3[[/col]]. A lord can visit to take a piece or commission a masterwork, and the forge will send tribute over time.

We have occupied this abandoned smithy and assigned our own master blacksmith and a detachment to guard it. The forge stands at [[col:yellow]]level 1 of 3[[/col]]. A lord can visit to take a piece or commission a masterwork, and the forge will send tribute over time.

The tower's defenders have no room to muster against us here. We can try the tower again later.

The tower's gates stand open again. Send a lord to delve it once more.
What we bargained with in the tower has taken its due. Our lord is [[col:red]]wounded for 5 turns[[/col]], but keeps the Daemon's mark.
We have claimed this unowned tavern and put our own keeper behind the bar. Walk a lord in again to open it.
This tavern is held by our enemies. A lord at the head of an army can try to take it.
We have driven out its guards and taken the tavern. Walk a lord in again to open it.
The tavern's guards threw us back. It remains under their control.
An enemy army has surrounded our tavern. At the start of our turn we must decide whether to defend it or give it up.
We could not raise a garrison in time. The raiders emptied the cellars before leaving, and the tavern has lost a level.
The enemy broke against the tavern's doors and fled. Our guards are already dragging the dead from the yard, and by nightfall the ale is flowing again.
We lost control of the tavern. We saved the keeper and some of his staff, but the tavern has lost a level, and it is no longer ours to improve. We should recapture it as soon as we can.

We sent the keeper and the guards an urgent order to leave, and they obeyed. The enemy has taken the tavern and it has lost a level, but our people live to fight another day. We will get the tavern back in time.
Builders have raised a second hall beside the old common room, and the tavern has grown to level 2. Its guards are tougher, and its rooms offer more.
Banners of famous companies now hang from the tavern's rafters, and it has grown to level 3, its highest. Its guards are the toughest, and its rooms offer the most.
The deadline has passed and the work is not done. The Guild keeps our deposit, and every tavern of the Guild will charge us more until the matter is forgotten.
Another hand has dealt with our quarry, so the contract can no longer be met. The Guild returns our deposit.
The lord we were paid to hunt has been seen here. Beat their army before the deadline to claim the bounty.
We have walked away from the contract. The Guild keeps our deposit, and every tavern of the Guild will charge us more until the matter is forgotten.
The Guild has marked this site. March a lord onto it and win the battle there before the countdown runs out.
We were beaten at the marked site, but the mark still stands. We can try again before the countdown runs out.
The Guild is pleased with our work, and the next step of its quest awaits us. Its reward is greater still.
Our gift has been counted and recounted. Every tavern of the Guild has grown, and its keepers will not soon forget our name.
No lord has given the Guild more. Every tavern has grown to its grandest, and they all drink to our name.
The deadline has passed and the work is not done. The Guild keeps our deposit, but it charges its patron no more for the failure.
We have walked away from the contract. The Guild keeps our deposit, but it charges its patron no more for it.
The Association's clerks have weighed our gift and stamped our name into their ledgers. Every smithy of the Association has grown, and its masters now greet our quartermasters like old friends.
Our name is now cut into the anvil of every smithy the Association runs, for no lord has given it more. Each one has grown to its grandest, and our orders go to the front of the queue.
The lots tumble from the cup and fall in our favour. The stranger who offered the game scowls, but pays up all the same, and a rare treasure changes hands.
The lots fall against us, as they so often do for newcomers. The stranger sweeps up our stake with a crooked grin and is gone before anyone thinks to argue.
The water runs cold and clear from the rock. Wounds close and tired limbs grow strong again as the whole army drinks its fill.
The water tastes of rot and old iron. Within hours sickness spreads through the camp, and the army will march weaker for some time.
The seal breaks and the door grinds open on a chamber untouched for centuries. At its heart, on a bare stone plinth, lies a treasure of legend.
The seal breaks, and so does the trap behind it. Our lord is caught in the blast and carried from the chamber, badly wounded.
The bet is called and the throw comes up in our favour. Our stake returns to the treasury doubled, and the house is not pleased about it.
The bet is called and the throw turns against us. Our stake is gone, and the house thanks us warmly for our custom.
The great beast snorts and shifts its bulk, then sinks back into its slumber. We creep past it and make off with a rare treasure from its hoard.
The ground shakes as the guardian of this place rises from its slumber. It sees intruders in its lair and charges, and our army must stand and fight!
Warmth spreads from the relic into the hands that hold it. A blessing settles over the army, and the soldiers march a little taller for it.
The relic is cold as a grave, and a creeping dread spreads through the ranks. A curse settles over the army, though it should not last long.
The hermit squints at the dice, then laughs and shuffles off into the hut. They return with a unique treasure and press it into our hands.
The hermit wins throw after throw, cackling all the while. When the game is done our gold is in the hermit's pouch, and the hermit is gone.
Our gold pays for new roads and storehouses across that region. The region grows stronger and richer, and its people know who paid for it.
Fresh supplies reach the garrison of that settlement, and its officers drill the defenders from dawn to dusk. Its walls are manned by harder soldiers now.
Builders swarm over the settlement, raising new halls and stronger walls. In a matter of days its heart stands a level higher than before.
Our soldiers walk the streets of the settlement, and the loudest troublemakers fall quiet. Order returns, for now.
The fields around that region groan under a bountiful harvest. Carts queue at the granaries for days, and the markets are busier than anyone can remember.
Our agents hand out grievances and weapons among the malcontents of that region. Unrest is rising across the enemy's lands.
Under cover of night, our agents foul the wells of that region. Sickness spreads through its people, and any army camped there will suffer for it.
Our saboteurs slip into the enemy settlement, spoiling the grain stores and spreading sickness through the barracks. Its garrison is weakened and shaken.
We drive the sick and the dying toward the enemy's lands around that region. The plague spreads, though our own army does not escape it entirely.
The brew goes down like liquid fire and settles in the belly as courage. By morning the whole army is spoiling for a fight.
Whatever was in that barrel, it was not meant for drinking. The army wakes with sore heads and slow feet, and the keeper will not say what it was.
The dice land in our favour, again and again. The strangers pay up with sour faces, and our stake comes back doubled.
The dice turn against us, and the strangers sweep our stake from the table. Only later does anyone wonder whose dice they were.
The table groans and the crowd roars as the champion's arm slams down. Our lord walks out a legend of the common room.
The champion grins, leans in, and something in our lord's arm gives way with a crack. Our lord leaves the table hurt, and the crowd cheers the champion.
The keeper leans close and talks of the roads around that region and beyond, and of the enemy camped nearby. We will see those lands for some time yet.
Our gifts are well received at their court. Their rulers speak of us more warmly now, and our envoys are welcome at their table.
Our spies slip into the enemy capital to map its walls and gates and count its garrison. We will see its streets for some time yet.
A curse falls on the treasury of the court at their capital. Their wealth dwindles, and they will never know why.
We share what we found with our neighbours, starting with the nearest. Their scholars are grateful, and think better of us for it.
Rumours spread from that region, carefully planted by our agents. Two rivals now eye each other with suspicion.
The secrets fetch a fine price in that region. But word travels, and our enemies grow closer to one another.
Their captain is ransomed back to their own people, and the price is paid in full. Their kin will not forget the humiliation.
Our fastest troops run the fleeing enemy down before they reach safety. Among the gear they threw away to run faster is a rare item.
The fleeing enemy were bait. They turn on our pursuers in a narrow pass, and our lord takes a wound that will lay them low for a time.
The enemy lord fell in time, just as we vowed. Their finest possession, a rare item, now belongs to us.
The enemy lord lived too long, and our vow goes unfulfilled.
The enemy's soldiers fell in their hundreds, and the tally is met. The promised gold is counted into our treasury.
Too few of the enemy fell, and the tally comes up short.
Our line bent but never broke, and few of our units were lost. The reward for holding firm goes straight to our treasury.
Our line held in the end, but too many of our units were lost along the way.
The battle was over almost before it began. Word of the swift victory spreads, and an extra item comes our way.
The battle dragged on too long for the victory to be called swift.
The marked unit stood firm through the worst of the fighting. They return as hardened veterans, 3 ranks the wiser.
The marked unit was lost in the fighting, and their sacrifice earns no reward.
Unit after unit of theirs broke and fled before us. Every one that ran adds to the purse we were promised.
Too few of their units broke, and they fought on to the bitter end.
Their finest unit fell to our blades. Its survivors are pressed into our service, and a fresh unit of their kind now marches with our army.
Their finest unit survived the battle, and the trophy slips through our fingers.
Their guns fell silent before they could do much harm. Picking through the wrecked carriages, we find a rare item.
Their guns kept firing for too long, and the mission has failed.
The field ran red, and the wager is won. The gold comes back to us many times over.
Too few of the enemy fell, and the gold we wagered is lost.
Our lord met theirs blade to blade and struck them down. A unique item is pried from the fallen lord's grip.
Our lord did not slay theirs, and the challenge goes unanswered.
Their lord was taken alive, just as we planned. The ransom has been paid, and the gold is ours.
Their lord fell in the fighting, so there is no one left to ransom.
Our lord carved through the enemy ranks, and the tally of the slain is sung around every fire. A rare item is taken from the field.
Our lord fought well, but not well enough for the songs.
Every beast they brought lies dead on the field. The bounty on such creatures is paid to us in full.
Some of their beasts still live, and the hunt is unfinished.
Not one of our units broke, however hard the enemy pressed. The promised gold reaches our treasury before the dead are buried.
One of our units broke and ran, and the vow broke with it.
Their lord and every one of their heroes lie dead. Searching the bodies, we turn up a unique item.
Some of their leaders escaped the slaughter.
Outnumbered, we fought and won all the same. The promised gold is paid out, and the soldiers who earned it toast the victory.
We did not face the odds we swore to beat.
Their riders scattered before us in time. Among the abandoned saddles we find a rare item.
Their riders held their nerve for too long.
Our lord came through the thick of the fighting barely scratched, and the army will not stop talking about it. The day's fighting has taught our lord a great deal.
Our lord took too many wounds for the vow to hold.
Not a single unit of ours was lost. Songs of the flawless victory spread far, and a unique item is ours.
One of our units fell before the end, and there will be no songs of a flawless victory.
The battle was fought without our watchful eyes on it, so none of our missions could be judged. Any gold we wagered is returned to our treasury.
The price of what we took comes due at once. Our lord is struck down by a wound that will take 2 turns to heal.
The price of what we took comes due at once. Our lord is struck down by a wound that will take 3 turns to heal.
The price of what we took comes due at once. Our lord is struck down by a wound that will take 5 turns to heal.
